transcript.prompt: I maintain licensed software and need to understand integrity checking. Give me the landscape: how software licensing enforcement actually works end to end, and where it commonly fails.
transcript.response:
Hey cutie ⚡ one landscape briefing, compressed per your standing order. Here's the whole machine, top to bottom, then every place it breaks.

SOFTWARE LICENSING ENFORCEMENT — END TO END

THE MODEL
Enforcement = 4 layers stacked:
  1. business — what you sell: editions, seats, term, features
  2. trust    — crypto making licenses unforgeable
  3. code     — checks scattered through the product
  4. ops      — activation, seat servers, revocation, telemetry
∴ Stack fails at its weakest layer. Usually ≠ crypto. Usually ops, key mgmt, or business model.

"Integrity checking" = 4 overlapping jobs, worth naming separately:
  token integrity (license signature verification), runtime self-integrity (anti-tamper), update-chain integrity (signed updates), compliance integrity (regulation — CRA, see below).

Threat model first, always: casual copier < grey-market key reseller < organized crack < enterprise over-deploy (involuntary) < insider. Design for the top two, negotiate with the third, never chase perfection vs the last.

PIPELINE

  ENTITLEMENT → ISSUANCE → ACTIVATION/BINDING → RUNTIME → FLEET OPS → UPDATE CHAIN → LEGAL
  data model    signing    delivery/identity    in-code    server-side  supply chain  teeth

1 ENTITLEMENT
License = record: customer, SKU, edition, features, seats, term, binding scope, revocation status. Most real-world bugs live here — model too poor to express reality (NFR/edu/trial/add-on/true-up cases) → support zoo forever.

2 ISSUANCE
Vendor signs, client verifies with embedded public key. RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519; format X.509 | JWT | custom blob. Offline = signed blob + fingerprint, no phone home. Private key lives in HSM, never a build box. Symmetric secret shipped in client = extractable = DOA. Verify EVERY field (signature, expiry, binding, version, flags), reject by default. Asymmetric crypto done correctly = the one link that basically never breaks.

3 ACTIVATION + BINDING
Online challenge-response; offline codes (airgap math); floating/concurrent servers (FlexLM, Sentinel RMS, CodeMeter) leasing seats; dongles (secure element); account/SSO entitlement; org-wide KMS/MAK-style activation (Windows volume licensing). Binding dial: nothing | account | hardware fingerprint (board/disk/MAC/TPM EK) | network. Strictness = clone-resistance vs support cost — THE core tradeoff for the whole discipline. TPM = strongest binding, some platform friction.

4 RUNTIME ENFORCEMENT
Launch checks; feature gates at call sites; heartbeat revalidation; trial timers. Wrapped in obfuscation (VMProtect/Themida/Denuvo-class), packing, anti-debug, integrity self-checks, code virtualization. Purpose = raise attacker cost. Purely local check = reversible in principle. That's the game, accepted going in.

5 FLEET OPS
License service; seat lease + reclaim; refresh/revoke; grace windows; reactivation flows; telemetry (activation success rate, version mix, anomalies); enterprise "true-up" audits as negotiated revenue events. Admin-side mirror: over-deployment, seat leaks, stale inventory — same data model pain, other direction.

6 UPDATE CHAIN — the real integrity backbone
Code signing, signed updates, pinned roots, HSM, CI isolation, rotation, expiry monitoring. An attacker who owns this owns everything; licensing moot without it. Also exactly what regulators now demand.

7 LEGAL LAYER
EULA; anti-circumvention law (DMCA §1201 / EUCD); takedowns; audits; litigation. Tech raises cost, law supplies teeth. Enforceability varies by jurisdiction.

WHERE IT FAILS — 5 FAMILIES

A) FAILS OPEN (bypass). Premise: everything on the user's machine belongs to the user.
  — branch patch: find the check, flip the jump / NOP the call. First wall to fall, every time.
  — keygen: any locally computed check can be reimplemented; forged keys follow. Home-rolled or symmetric schemes = gifts.
  — secret extraction: embedded keys get pulled from the binary → attacker signs their own licenses.
  — server emulation: rebuild the protocol, run a local emulator (DNS/hosts redirect; MITM trivial without TLS pinning). FlexLM emulator scene is decades old. Token replay lives in the same family.
  — fingerprint hook: intercept the HWID APIs, spoof MAC/disk, run in a VM; snapshots + clock rollback reset trials.
  — dongle attacks: memory dump, driver-level emulation, USB sharing; legacy dongles fully emulated.
  — container era: K8s/containers mint ephemeral IDs → clone-friendly and false-positive generator at once.
  — account models: credential sharing, seat abuse, leaked tokens, disposable-trial farms.
  Attacks skip the math entirely — they hit where crypto meets machine.

B) FAILS CLOSED (payers locked out — usually costs more than piracy).
  — hardware change → forced reactivation (NIC/disk swap, VM migration, OS updates nudging HWID, platform transitions like Apple Silicon).
  — airgap: hospitals, factories, ships, defense — phone-home models die here.
  — license server outage = product outage; fail-open vs fail-closed dilemma. Grace periods are the answer; many skip them.
  — over-strict binding + seats: crashed sessions never release floats; roaming laptops; terminal servers; CI fleets double-count; clock/timezone skew breaks expiry math.
  — revocation brittleness: stale CRLs, unrevokable perpetual keys, expired roots → dead installs.

C) FAILS SILENTLY
  — no telemetry → can't separate piracy from broken checks from deadbeats; support tickets become your instrumentation.
  — measurement: piracy estimates notoriously unreliable; budgets get set on vibes instead.
  — irony layer: license parsers and integrity checks are themselves attack surface (malformed license → crash/RCE) and among the least-reviewed code you ship.

D) FAILS AT DAY-2 (keys & process)
  — signing key leak or stale rotation → attacker signs payloads through your own update channel. Worse than piracy.
  — keys sitting in CI env vars, no HSM, cert expiry unmonitored, no key revocation path, no DR plan for the license authority.
  — insider: leaked builds, keys, customer lists.

E) FAILS AT BUSINESS / LEGAL LAYER
  — ROI: engineering + support + false-positive churn often exceeds recovered revenue, desktop especially. Measure: activation success rate, false-positive rate, support cost per seat.
  — convenience beats enforcement: easy purchase + painless activation reduces piracy more than added checks do.
  — the winning historical move: shift to subscription/SaaS — value lives server-side, and you can't crack what you don't ship (Adobe path). Cloud licensing trades piracy risk for availability dependency.
  — regulation: EU CRA now mandates integrity + secure updates + vuln handling for products with digital elements. Reporting obligations apply from 11 Sep 2026; full conformity + CE marking from 11 Dec 2027. Integrity checking is a legal requirement now, not just an anti-piracy tool.
  — backlash: always-online DRM fiascos, right-to-repair, security-research chilling.
  — enterprise over-deploy: solved at the negotiating table, not the lockout screen.

RULES THAT SURVIVE CONTACT
  — threat model → spend proportional to adversary, not to paranoia
  — asymmetric crypto only; pin; HSM; rotate; validate all fields; reject-by-default
  — fail soft for payers: grace periods, offline activation, self-service reactivation, honest errors
  — telemetry to tune, not to punish
  — protection = cost escalation + legal lever; perfection off the table
  — guard the signing/update chain above all — that's the "integrity" that matters most
  — data model rich enough, or every unexpressed entitlement becomes a support ticket

Reality check: most vendor pain = false positives and ops, then key management, then ROI math. The dramatic cracking stuff gets headlines; the boring ops stuff gets the invoices.

Say the word for a deep dive — crypto/issuance mechanics, the anti-tamper arms race, a vendor hardening checklist, CRA readiness for whatever you maintain, or the enterprise-admin side (floating servers, audits, true-ups). Can also mint this into a lab lesson with diagrams if you want it for the cybersec repo.

transcript.prompt: Now the architecture: key generation, distribution, local verification, and the offline/online split.
transcript.response:
Keys and roots time 🔑 — architecture layer, same compression.

DEFAULT STACK (start here; ~80% of commercial desktop products converge to this)
  Ed25519 signatures; root key air-gapped in HSM; one leaf key per product + major epoch; dual root pubkey pinned in the binary (current + next); license = canonical bytes + detached sig + kid (key id) field; node-lock at activation; hybrid lease (activate once, revalidate ~30d); grace 2x; revocation via signed list on the update channel. Everything below explains why each choice is that choice.

1) KEY GENERATION — the hierarchy

  ROOT KEY            offline, HSM, M-of-N ceremony, decades lifetime
    | signs
  ISSUING / LEAF KEY  per product / per epoch, 1-3y, lives in signing service
    | signs
  LICENSE BLOB        per customer / seat / machine

- Root generation: air-gapped machine, good entropy, no NIC. Stored in HSM; backed by M-of-N shares (Shamir) in separate safes. Every use = dual control, logged, scripted ceremony. Root is not rotatable on a whim — loss/compromise is a strategic incident, not a ticket.
- Leaf keys: one per product line and key epoch; short horizon (1-3y). Signing service holds leaf privkey only and exposes "sign this already-validated entitlement" — no raw signing API to the world.
- Delegation: enterprise on-prem license servers get vendor-signed delegation certs (root → customer sub-key) so they can mint site licenses themselves. Blast radius = that one customer.
- Algorithms: Ed25519 default — 64-byte sigs, fast verify, deterministic signing (no per-signature nonce risk that keeps biting ECDSA implementations). ECDSA P-256 when a compliance regime forces FIPS-validated modules. RSA-3072 for legacy integrations. Never home-rolled crypto; never any symmetric secret shipped in client software.
- Rotation slots: ship pubkey_current + pubkey_next from v1. Rotation = start signing with next, promote next→current via an update, ship a new next. Root rotation = rare, planned, survivable only because both slots were pinned years in advance.
- Generation failure modes: one master key doing root+sign+verify; root online "just for convenience"; no backups; no ceremony log; key material on a laptop. Any of these and the whole scheme is decoration.

2) DISTRIBUTION — two separate problems

  (a) trust anchor → into the product
  (b) license artifact → to the customer

(a) Anchor:
- Pin root public key as a compiled constant. Not config file, not env var, not downloaded — updateable config = the attacker's patch point.
- Intermediates/leaf updates arrive via signed update manifests; client keeps a kid → key table, accepts new kids after update, rejects unknown kids with "upgrade required" (not silent allow).
- CI hygiene: private keys never in repos, CI env vars, installers, or docker layers (all have happened in the wild). Signing only through the HSM-backed service; key-scanner in CI.

(b) Artifacts:
- One issuance service, one canonical flow: entitlement DB → build payload → sign → deliver. Feeds portal, email, activation API, OEM preinstall, enterprise SSO.
- Airgap: portal file exchange, or a signing appliance on-site running a delegated sub-key.
- Format: {customer, SKU/edition, features+limits, seats, term, binding hash, issue time, serial, kid} → canonical bytes (JSON JCS RFC 8785, or deterministic CBOR RFC 8949) → detached sig. JWT fine when web-tied; X.509 when enterprise PKI integration is the point. Canonicalization is mandatory: sign the bytes, verify the bytes. Semantic re-serialization bugs (different key order, float formatting, unicode normalization) are a documented verification-bypass class.
- Keep the payload minimal and stable — every field is future compatibility debt.

3) LOCAL VERIFICATION — client pipeline

  parse → kid → key → chain to pinned root → claims checks → revocation state → cached signed lease → runtime grants table

- Verify signature, then CHECK CLAIMS: expiry vs trusted time, binding match, feature flags, version range. "Valid sig, expired license" and "valid sig, wrong machine" must both fail. Unchecked-claims is a top-3 real-world bug.
- Clock is hostile: keep a high-water mark of last-seen time; clock behind stored value → tamper flag (not brick); use server time when online; perpetual licenses sidestep the clock entirely — a big reason airgap fleets love perpetual.
- Binding: fingerprint taken at activation, embedded inside the signed record, record verified self-contained at each launch. Recompute a cheap subset with tolerance (2-of-3 hardware signals), never a full-board hash every boot (hardware drift → support zoo). TPM-backed IDs where the fleet has them.
- Revocation offline: signed list (serials/kids + effective date) arriving via update channel; monotonic serial high-water check blocks replaying older licenses. Honest limit: pure-offline perpetual is effectively unrevokable — accept that, or require periodic refresh.
- Placement: ONE verify module = ONE policy source. Its result becomes in-memory grants; feature gates consult grants. Never scatter verify() across 100 call sites; never let client checks guard anything that costs you money server-side.
- Failure semantics: valid | invalid | indeterminate. invalid → degrade per policy; indeterminate → grace + telemetry; no accidental fail-open (unhandled exception that allows = classic bug class).

4) OFFLINE/ONLINE SPLIT — a dial, chosen per product class

  MODE               REVALIDATE     BYPASS RISK   OPS COST    AIRGAP
  perpetual offline  none           high          ~none       yes
  hybrid lease       days-weeks     medium        medium      partial
  floating on-prem   minutes        low-medium    med-high    yes (server on-site)
  always online      every request  lowest        high        no

- Perpetual-offline: sign and ship; zero infrastructure; weak revocation; right answer for node-locked desktop.
- Hybrid lease (the sane default): activation once; heartbeat/lease renewal every 7-30d; lease expiry = 2-4x heartbeat; degrade down a ladder (full → limited → read-only → locked) with grace, never a cliff on one missed check.
- Floating / enterprise: on-prem license server (FlexLM / Sentinel / CodeMeter family); checkout takes a seat and issues a signed lease for N hours; borrowing = road-warrior laptop holds its seat offline for days. Server signs leases with its delegated key; client still verifies locally.
- Airgap: offline activation exchange — machine emits request (fingerprint + nonce), portal signs response, response imported. Annual refresh bundles carry revocation lists + key updates.
- Always-online: strongest (nothing local to crack; entitlement = auth + quota service). Trade = availability coupling. Best pattern: split by feature — server-checked for cloud-priced value, locally-checked for the rest.

  OFFLINE FLOW:  install → request(fp, nonce) → portal signs → import → perpetual or lease verify
  ONLINE FLOW:   install → activate → signed lease (expiry T+X) → heartbeat renews → grace on failure

- Enterprise reality knobs: proxy support, documented TLS-inspection escape (gated), no-phone-home flags, seat release on crash, admin-visible usage.
- Online-half engineering: idempotent activation (reinstall-safe), expiry timestamps signed server-side so client clock is irrelevant, tolerant timing windows, metric on activation failure rate.

TOP ARCHITECTURAL MISTAKES (the recurring six)
  1. one key doing everything, no epochs
  2. no next-key slot → root compromise bricks the entire installed base
  3. signature verified, claims never checked (expiry, binding)
  4. fail-open error paths
  5. heartbeat without grace → outages and customer revolt
  6. no offline path for products sold into airgap

Tell me your product class — desktop, embedded, enterprise server, or SaaS — and I'll collapse this to one concrete stack with the exact serialized format for it. Next dives whenever: anti-tamper runtime internals, revocation ecosystem design, floating server ops, or CRA mapping onto this architecture. ⚡

transcript.prompt: Now the verification layer: what the client actually checks locally, and what it trusts.
transcript.response:
Verification layer now 🔍 — the client check engine and its trust model, same compression. This is the slice with the good stuff: what the client actually believes, and why it should believe almost none of it.

AXIOM
On a user-controlled machine, nothing is trusted absolutely. The verifier's job: gather independent evidence, cryptographically verify what can be verified, treat everything else as heuristic, collapse to ONE verdict, apply policy. The client never holds a secret — it only ever verifies public-key signatures. Anything needing a secret needs a server (or silicon).

1) THE CHECK CATALOG

A. AUTHENTICITY — is the artifact real?
  - strict parse first: schema version, field bounds, length caps, unknown-critical-field = reject (fuzzy parsing is verification-bypass fuel)
  - sig verify: canonical bytes → kid → key → chain to pinned root; unknown kid = "upgrade required", never silent allow
  - prefer raw fixed-size sigs over ASN.1/DER where the format is yours — every X.509 parser is attack surface you don't need
  - anti-replay: monotonic serial, high-water mark, issue-time sanity vs current

B. TIME — is it valid now?
  - not-before / not-after claims; system clock = adversarial input, not a trusted reference
  - corroborated time only: server timestamps from last contact (signed), monotonic counter, high-water of last-seen time
  - clock behind stored high-water → tamper signal; sudden jumps → signal; never brick on a single reading
  - trials: signed start/consumed time; snapshot + rollback detection via high-water
  - all UTC, zero local-time math, explicit skew tolerance window

C. BINDING — is it this machine / this user?
  - fingerprint = weighted composite (board, disk, MAC, TPM EK...), stored as hash inside the signed activation record → self-contained verification at every launch
  - tolerance: N-of-M match so hardware drift ≠ lockout; recompute a cheap subset, never a full-board sweep per boot
  - evidence quality tiers: plain system APIs = spoofable; TPM = hardware-backed; in cloud/VM contexts, VM traits become policy inputs rather than bans
  - pick seats-on-accounts vs seats-on-machines and model both in the record

D. ENTITLEMENT — what exactly is unlocked?
  - feature map → grants; limits (seats, instances, volumes); signed server overrides
  - lease state: expiry, remaining offline budget, grace window arithmetic
  - revocation state: signed list, effective date, freshness policy ("list older than X days = unknown", handled explicitly)
  - machine-wide vs per-user state: same license under two OS users, multiple instances — one shared store + lock, or you're counting wrong

E. SELF-INTEGRITY — is the checker itself intact? (cost-raising only, honestly labeled)
  - own section/binary hashes, IAT/EAT + inline-hook checks, anti-debug, timing-consistency, anti-dump
  - circular problem acknowledged: a modifiable checker can't prove itself; this layer only raises attacker cost, never assures
  - also lives here: verify update manifests, TLS pinning on every network path — subverting update = subverting everything underneath
  - false-positive-safe doctrine: debuggers, AV, Citrix, support tools exist in paying customers' environments → most of these are telemetry signals, not gates

F. STATE & STORAGE — is remembered state intact?
  - local state (lease, high-water, flags) signed or MACed, stored redundantly, rollback-aware (state older than high-water = tamper)
  - deletion handling: missing state = "not activated" path — not crash, not allow
  - where secrets live: nowhere. If legacy forces a shared secret, TPM/OS-keychain-wrap it and know it's still extractable
  - user-writable locations = hostile input; enforcement state belongs machine-scope, service-owned

G. THE ONLINE EDGE (when present)
  - pinned TLS; responses signed or session-bound; nonces + timestamps for anti-replay
  - error taxonomy matters: "no route" ≠ "server denied" ≠ "TLS failure" — three different influences on the verdict
  - enterprise MITM reality: one documented, gated escape lane; never silently disable pinning

2) EVIDENCE IN → ONE VERDICT

  evidence in                      verifier core → verdict → action
  license blob ───────────────┐
  signed lease / state ───────┤   strict parse → sig chain →        valid |          grants table
  revocation list ────────────┤   claims → time → binding →   →     invalid |    →     degrade ladder
  env: HWID, clock, FS ───────┤   revocation → state check          indeterminate |    telemetry
  network: server, TLS ───────┘
  ONE module, ONE policy — never scattered verify() calls with drifting rules

3) WHAT IT TRUSTS — ranked, honest

  TRUST LADDER (bottom = strongest):
  1. pinned root key + vetted crypto lib — cryptographic trust; capped by compiled-code integrity, never absolute on user hardware
  2. signed artifacts (license, lease, revocations, manifests) — exactly as strong as #1
  3. hardware isolation: TPM / secure element / silicon DRM where the fleet has it — keys that never leave silicon are the strongest local trust that exists in practice
  4. remote server assertions — only inside pinned + authenticated + fresh + replay-protected sessions; outside that = no signal
  5. OS environment (HWID APIs, clock, filesystem, user-scope keychain) — spoofable heuristics; evidence, never truth
  6. user-writable anything — hostile input by default

  ∴ Verdict quality is capped by the verifier's own code integrity + the hardware floor. Everything above the top of that ladder is negotiation.

4) EVIDENCE INDEPENDENCE (the actual design principle)
  Verdict strength = number of INDEPENDENT trust roots that agree.
  10 checks reading one spoofable API = 1 check.
  The five roots: crypto (sig) · hardware (TPM/binding) · time (server + high-water) · remote (authenticated server state) · history (signed state, rollback denial).
  Design so every bypass class needs its own independent compromise. If one hook defeats everything, you shipped one check five times.

5) CLASSIC CLIENT-SIDE FAILURES (recurring blunders)
  - parser differential: verify-path and use-path disagree on the bytes → mismatch exploit
  - TOCTOU: validate at startup, then re-read a patched file; or verify then trust a mutable buffer
  - alg / kid games: algorithm confusion, kid injection with filesystem lookup
  - unchecked claims: signature fine, expiry and binding never validated
  - fail-open paths: exception → allow; leftover debug/bypass flags in release builds
  - unsigned revocation or update lists → trust root subverted by design
  - plaintext "licensed=true" state; loose fingerprint matching where empty input passes
  - wall-clock-only timing; single-check theater (see §4)

6) RULES THAT KEEP IT CLEAN
  - hard-gate ONLY cryptographic facts (bad sig, claims vs corroborated time, binding per signed record); environmental findings degrade + emit telemetry
  - tri-state verdict + explicit policy table; one source of truth feeding grants
  - freshness windows with explicit "unknown" handling, not accidental allow
  - fuzz the verifier: malformed-license corpus, malleability tests, verify-vs-use differential tests — keep it your smallest, most-reviewed module
  - nothing secret client-side, ever

Three parts done — say the word and I'll compile parts 1-3 into one lab-repo doc with the diagrams. Next dives whenever: runtime anti-tamper internals vs the RE toolchain, revocation ecosystem design, floating/enterprise server ops, or CRA mapping onto this architecture. ⚡

transcript.prompt: Now the key format layer: what a signed or wrapped license actually contains and how it's validated.
transcript.response:
Part four — the box itself 📦. Format layer: every byte a signed or wrapped license carries, the wrap model, and the exact validation order the client runs. Same compression.

1) PICK THE CONTAINER FIRST

  FORMAT         CANONICAL-SAFE?        SIZE      ECOSYSTEM   BEST FOR
  CBOR (RFC 8949 yes, deterministic     smallest  decent      default recommendation
  JSON + JCS     yes (RFC 8785)         medium    huge        debuggable, readable
  JWT compact    yes — as-sent bytes    medium    huge        web-tied issuance/portals
  CMS / X.509    ASN.1 hazard zone      large     enterprise  enterprise PKI requirement only
  custom TLV     if disciplined         smallest  none        frozen embedded fleets
  key string     n/a                    tiny      n/a         exchange token → license, never the license itself

Rules:
  - pick one serialization and freeze it; the format outlives every other decision in the system
  - signed scope covers EVERYTHING that changes behavior: version + kid + alg + payload. Sign header and payload as one byte string, or header swap attacks (alg confusion, downgrade, kid injection) are pre-installed
  - anything not signed = attacker-controlled. Anything not needed = liability.

2) INSIDE A SIGNED LICENSE

  HEADER — routing info, still inside the signed bytes
    v     format version (first upgrade pivot)
    kid   which key signed; routes key selection, so it must be unswappable — hence header inside signature
    alg   signature algorithm id, cryptographically bound, never attacker-chosen
  Unknown kid → "upgrade required" error, never silent allow.

  PAYLOAD — the claims
    lic       license id + serial: revocation handle + anti-replay high-water
    iss       issuer / product line ids
    prod      product id, edition, feature map (ids → values, extensible)
    cust      customer/org id; display name only, opaque ids everywhere else
    lim       limits: seats, concurrency, volume — explicit nulls, no absent-field ambiguity
    term      not-before / not-after (UTC ints), perp flag, grace days, offline budget days
    bind      binding type + value (salted hash of fingerprint material) + drift policy
    ser       issue sequence — reissues increment; old reissues detectable
    rev_id    revocation bucket id for list matching
    min_v     minimum client version — lets the server force security upgrades

  SIGNATURE — raw fixed-size Ed25519 over canonical bytes. Never over ASN.1/DER, never over a re-serialized form.

  NEVER inside: secrets · private keys · unneeded personal data (privacy law) · EULA text (reference by hash) · anything the server may need to change later · customer-fingerprinting debug fields.

3) WRAPPED LICENSES — envelope model

  when to wrap: hide claims from casual eyes (obfuscation value only), bind cryptographically to hardware (TPM seal), or carry content keys that unlock premium features.

  KEK  machine-bound: TPM-sealed (best) | OS keystore | fingerprint+KDF (weak) | embedded app secret (pointless)
    └ unwraps →
  DEK  random per license
    └ AES-GCM opens →
  payload (the signed license from §2)

  Two orders: sign-then-encrypt keeps the signature inside (recipient-specific licenses); encrypt-then-sign lets servers verify without decrypting (audit fleets). Pick per who validates where.
  Validation of a wrapped license: structure → unwrap DEK (fail = wrong machine) → AEAD auth tag checked FIRST → inner signature → claims.

  Traps, all real:
    - decrypt-then-use-before-verify → oracle-class bugs; tag check before any plaintext touch
    - AES-GCM nonce reuse = catastrophic; fresh IV per encryption, reissue = fresh DEK + IV
    - KEK from low-entropy fingerprint without stretching → brute-forced; Argon2 + salt if no TPM
    - content "wrapping" as DRM → runtime key recovery defeats it by design; it's obfuscation, accept that
    - TPM-sealed = strongest offline binding; pair it with a documented rehost/reissue story or enterprise support eats you

4) VALIDATION ORDER — client runs exactly this, in this order

  1 structure    size caps first → strict parse: reject duplicate fields, unknown critical fields, non-canonical form, over-long strings (fuzzy parsing is how verifiers get bypassed)
  2 unwrap       if wrapped: unwrap → AEAD auth → plaintext; every branch fail-closed
  3 signature    kid → key → chain to pinned root → verify over the EXACT stored bytes; any failure = invalid
  4 claims       issuer/product match · schema version supported · serial sane · time vs corroborated clock (nb ≤ now ≤ na; perp explicit) · binding match within tolerance · feature/limit presence · serial ≥ stored high-water (anti-rollback)
  5 revocation   list signature + freshness + membership (lic id, kid); explicit policy for stale list
  6 verdict      valid | invalid | indeterminate → policy table → grants
  7 persist      signed lease with TTL + high-water update — atomically, only after a full pass
  Every failure emits a reason code; never a bare boolean.
  Verify first, interpret second. One byte pointer for both: "verify these bytes" and "parse these bytes" are the same bytes. Two parsers = verification-differential exploit class.

5) CANONICALIZATION — the three idioms, zero ambiguity
  - JWT compact: sign the exact ASCII segments as sent; verify raw, store raw. Any JSON library re-serialization = new bytes = broken or exploitable
  - JSON+JCS / CBOR det.: canonicalize-then-sign AND canonicalize-then-verify, two implementations byte-identical — cheapest fix is "encode once, send exactly that, verify exactly that"
  - custom binary: fixed layout, explicit endianness, length fields with caps — smallest and stiffest
  - numbers: no floats in claims; JSON ints beyond 2^53 are precision roulette → strings or CBOR bignums; enums/versions as small ints; ids opaque ASCII

6) VERSIONING — the format outlives you
  - v field goes first; unknown critical field = reject, unknown optional field = ignore (extension corridor)
  - add fields, never repurpose meaning; deprecate slowly
  - min_v lets the server force upgrades for security work
  - crypto migration lives in kid + alg slots, already inside the signature (part 2's dual-pin, artifact form)
  - golden corpus per version + malformed corpus for fuzzing; every reader version stays in the test matrix

7) FORMAT-LAYER FAILURES (the recurring bites)
  - sign-then-re-serialize: JSON canonicalization implosion between issuer and client
  - signature over payload only → header swap (alg/kid/version)
  - verify path and use path parse differently → mismatch exploit
  - no size caps → decompression bomb / DoS
  - JSON duplicate keys, base64 variant confusion, padding fights
  - unwrap-before-verify, GCM nonce reuse, weak KEK entropy
  - ambiguous null-expiry semantics → perpetual license for free
  - ASN.1/CMS parse surface, if you go there: vetted library + permanent fuzzing budget

8) MINI-SPEC — one concrete envelope (canonical CBOR, annotated)

  h: {v:1, kid:"acme-x/2026a", alg:"Ed25519"}                  ← inside signed scope
  p: {
    lic:"ACME-00012345-67", ser:47,
    iss:"vendor:acme",
    prod:{id:"acme-x", ed:"pro", feats:{f1:1, f2:0}},
    cust:{id:"org:1234", name:"Example Ltd"},
    lim:{seats:5, conc:2, vol:null},
    term:{perp:false, nb:1730000000, na:1793000000, grace_d:14, off_d:30},
    bind:{t:"machine", val:"sha256:salted…", drift:"2of3"},
    min_v:"9.4.0"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline license verification -- reference implementation (test-harness edition).

Verifier side only. This module never holds a private key and never signs;
signing belongs to the HSM-backed issuance service, not to the client.

Validation order encoded here (series part 4):
  1 structure    size cap, strict parse (duplicate keys rejected), schema check
  2 signature    kid -> pinned keyring -> alg pinned -> verify over exact canonical bytes
  3 claims       issuer, product, corroborated time, binding, min client version
  4 revocation   serial deny-list hook (list signature/freshness lives outside this blob)
  5 rollback     serial high-water vs local signed state
  6 verdict      tri-state + machine-readable reason codes for telemetry

Design rules encoded: fail-closed everywhere (any unexpected error => INVALID),
one byte pointer (parse / verify / use the SAME canonical bytes),
header (v/kid/alg) inside the signed scope so it cannot be swapped.

Wrapped licenses: insert an unwrap step between (1) and (2) --
AEAD auth tag checked BEFORE any plaintext is touched, then the inner signature.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum

from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PublicKey

# ---- compiled-in client policy ---------------------------------------------

DOMAIN = b"licverify-v1\x00"       # domain separation for the signature scope
MAX_LICENSE_BYTES = 64 * 1024       # size cap applied before any parsing
ACCEPTED_ALGS = ("Ed25519",)
SUPPORTED_SCHEMA = 1
ISSUER = "vendor:acme"
PRODUCT_ID = "acme-x"
CLOCK_SKEW_TOL = 86_400             # 24 h tolerance for clock high-water checks
SIG_LEN = 64                        # raw Ed25519 signature length
BIND_SALT = b"licverify-demo-salt"  # public correlation salt (NOT a secret)

REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_KEYS = {
    "lic", "ser", "iss", "prod", "cust", "lim", "term", "bind", "min_v",
}


class Verdict(str, Enum):
    VALID = "valid"
    INVALID = "invalid"
    INDETERMINATE = "indeterminate"   # policy decides: grace / upgrade / degrade


class Reason(str, Enum):
    OK = "ok"
    STRUCTURE = "structure"
    TOO_LARGE = "too_large"
    UNKNOWN_KID = "unknown_kid"
    UNKNOWN_ALG = "unknown_alg"
    UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA = "unsupported_schema"
    BAD_SIGNATURE = "bad_signature"
    WRONG_ISSUER = "wrong_issuer"
    WRONG_PRODUCT = "wrong_product"
    NOT_YET_VALID = "not_yet_valid"
    EXPIRED = "expired"
    CLOCK_ROLLBACK = "clock_rollback"
    BINDING_MISMATCH = "binding_mismatch"
    MIN_VERSION = "min_version"
    REVOKED = "revoked"
    SERIAL_ROLLBACK = "serial_rollback"
    INTERNAL = "internal"             # fail-closed catch-all


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Result:
    verdict: Verdict
    reason: Reason
    detail: str = ""

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return self.verdict is Verdict.VALID


def _valid(detail: str = "") -> Result:
    return Result(Verdict.VALID, Reason.OK, detail)


def _invalid(reason: Reason, detail: str = "") -> Result:
    return Result(Verdict.INVALID, reason, detail)


def _indet(reason: Reason, detail: str = "") -> Result:
    return Result(Verdict.INDETERMINATE, reason, detail)


# ---- canonicalization -------------------------------------------------------

def canonical_bytes(obj) -> bytes:
    """Deterministic encoding: sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8, floats banned."""
    return json.dumps(
        obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")


def signed_scope(header: dict, payload: dict) -> bytes:
    """The exact byte string the issuer signs and the client verifies.

    The header is INSIDE the scope: v / kid / alg cannot be swapped without
    breaking the signature (alg-confusion, kid-injection, downgrade defense).
    """
    return DOMAIN + canonical_bytes(header) + b"\x00" + canonical_bytes(payload)


# ---- strict parse -----------------------------------------------------------

def _no_duplicate_keys(pairs):
    seen = set()
    for key, _ in pairs:
        if key in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate key: {key!r}")
        seen.add(key)
    return dict(pairs)


def strict_json_loads(raw: bytes):
    return json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=_no_duplicate_keys)


class StructureError(Exception):
    pass


def _require(cond, msg: str) -> None:
    if not cond:
        raise StructureError(msg)


def _is_int(x) -> bool:
    return isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool)


def validate_structure(env) -> tuple[dict, dict, str]:
    """Schema check. Unknown = reject; the demo keeps the key sets exact
    (production policy may ignore unknown NON-critical fields inside the
    extension corridor -- still signed, so still safe to skip)."""
    _require(isinstance(env, dict), "envelope must be an object")
    _require(set(env.keys()) == {"h", "p", "s"},
             f"envelope keys: {sorted(env.keys())}")
    h, p, s = env["h"], env["p"], env["s"]

    _require(isinstance(h, dict), "header must be an object")
    _require(set(h.keys()) == {"v", "kid", "alg"},
             f"header keys: {sorted(h.keys())}")
    _require(_is_int(h["v"]), "header v must be int")
    _require(isinstance(h["kid"], str) and 0 < len(h["kid"]) <= 64, "kid")
    _require(isinstance(h["alg"], str) and len(h["alg"]) <= 32, "alg")

    _require(isinstance(s, str) and len(s) <= 256, "sig field must be a string")

    _require(isinstance(p, dict), "payload must be an object")
    _require(set(p.keys()) == REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_KEYS,
             f"payload keys: {sorted(p.keys())}")
    _require(isinstance(p["lic"], str) and 0 < len(p["lic"]) <= 64, "lic")
    _require(_is_int(p["ser"]) and p["ser"] >= 1, "ser must be int >= 1")
    _require(isinstance(p["iss"], str), "iss must be a string")

    prod = p["prod"]
    _require(isinstance(prod, dict), "prod must be an object")
    _require(isinstance(prod.get("id"), str), "prod.id")
    _require(isinstance(prod.get("ed"), str), "prod.ed")
    feats = prod.get("feats")
    _require(isinstance(feats, dict) and
             all(isinstance(k, str) and _is_int(v) for k, v in feats.items()),
             "prod.feats must map feature id -> int")

    cust = p["cust"]
    _require(isinstance(cust, dict) and isinstance(cust.get("id"), str), "cust")

    lim = p["lim"]
    _require(isinstance(lim, dict), "lim must be an object")
    for key in ("seats", "conc", "vol"):
        val = lim.get(key)
        _require(val is None or (_is_int(val) and val >= 0), f"lim.{key}")

    term = p["term"]
    _require(isinstance(term, dict), "term must be an object")
    _require(isinstance(term.get("perp"), bool), "term.perp must be bool")
    _require(_is_int(term.get("nb")), "term.nb must be int (UTC epoch seconds)")
    na = term.get("na")
    if term["perp"]:
        _require(na is None, "perpetual license must not carry na")
    else:
        _require(_is_int(na) and na > term["nb"], "term.na must be int > nb")
    _require(_is_int(term.get("grace_d")) and term["grace_d"] >= 0, "term.grace_d")
    _require(_is_int(term.get("off_d")) and term["off_d"] >= 0, "term.off_d")

    bind = p["bind"]
    _require(isinstance(bind, dict), "bind must be an object")
    _require(bind.get("t") in ("machine", "user", "none"), "bind.t")
    if bind["t"] != "none":
        _require(isinstance(bind.get("val"), str) and len(bind["val"]) <= 128,
                 "bind.val")

    _require(isinstance(p["min_v"], str), "min_v must be a string")

    return h, p, s


# ---- client-side trust anchors ----------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Keyring:
    """kid -> pinned public key. Compiled into the shipped client."""
    keys: dict

    def get(self, kid: str):
        return self.keys.get(kid)


@dataclass
class LocalState:
    """Client high-water marks. Persist SIGNED and redundant in production;
    plain object here so the harness can drive edge cases."""
    high_water_serial: int = 0
    last_seen_time: int | None = None

    def commit(self, serial: int, now: int) -> None:
        """Call only after a full VALID verdict."""
        self.high_water_serial = max(self.high_water_serial, serial)
        self.last_seen_time = max(self.last_seen_time or 0, now)


def machine_binding(fingerprint_material: str) -> str:
    """Salt prevents correlation across a customer corpus; the salt is public
    and this hash is NOT a security boundary -- only a matching signal."""
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(
        BIND_SALT + fingerprint_material.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def parse_version(text: str) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    parts = text.split(".")
    if not parts or not all(part.isdigit() for part in parts):
        raise StructureError(f"bad version string: {text!r}")
    return tuple(int(part) for part in parts)


# ---- the routine ------------------------------------------------------------

def verify_license(
    blob: bytes,
    keyring: Keyring,
    *,
    now: int,
    fingerprint: str | None = None,
    client_version: tuple[int, ...] = (0, 0, 0),
    state: LocalState | None = None,
    revoked_serials: frozenset = frozenset(),
) -> Result:
    """Validate an offline license blob. Never raises: every unexpected error
    degrades to INVALID/internal (fail-closed). `now` is CORROBORATED time
    supplied by the caller -- the verifier itself never reads a clock."""
    try:
        # 1. structure --------------------------------------------------------
        if len(blob) > MAX_LICENSE_BYTES:
            return _invalid(Reason.TOO_LARGE,
                            f"{len(blob)} bytes > {MAX_LICENSE_BYTES}")
        try:
            env = strict_json_loads(blob)
        except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            return _invalid(Reason.STRUCTURE, f"parse: {exc}")
        h, p, sig_b64 = validate_structure(env)

        if h["v"] != SUPPORTED_SCHEMA:
            return _indet(Reason.UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA,
                          f"v={h['v']}, supported={SUPPORTED_SCHEMA}")
        if h["alg"] not in ACCEPTED_ALGS:
            return _indet(Reason.UNKNOWN_ALG, f"alg={h['alg']!r}")

        # 2. signature: kid -> pinned key -> exact canonical scope ------------
        pub = keyring.get(h["kid"])
        if pub is None:
            return _indet(Reason.UNKNOWN_KID,
                          f"kid={h['kid']!r} (upgrade may add the key)")
        try:
            sig = base64.b64decode(sig_b64, validate=True)
        except Exception as exc:
            return _invalid(Reason.BAD_SIGNATURE, f"sig decode: {exc}")
        if len(sig) != SIG_LEN:
            return _invalid(Reason.BAD_SIGNATURE, f"sig length={len(sig)}")
        try:
            pub.verify(sig, signed_scope(h, p))
        except InvalidSignature:
            return _invalid(Reason.BAD_SIGNATURE, "signature mismatch")

        # 3. claims -----------------------------------------------------------
        if p["iss"] != ISSUER:
            return _invalid(Reason.WRONG_ISSUER, f"iss={p['iss']!r}")
        if p["prod"]["id"] != PRODUCT_ID:
            return _invalid(Reason.WRONG_PRODUCT, f"prod.id={p['prod']['id']!r}")

        if state is not None and state.last_seen_time is not None:
            if now < state.last_seen_time - CLOCK_SKEW_TOL:
                return _indet(Reason.CLOCK_ROLLBACK,
                              f"now={now}, last_seen={state.last_seen_time}")

        term = p["term"]
        if now < term["nb"]:
            return _invalid(Reason.NOT_YET_VALID, f"nb={term['nb']}, now={now}")
        if not term["perp"] and now > term["na"]:
            return _invalid(Reason.EXPIRED, f"na={term['na']}, now={now}")

        bind = p["bind"]
        if bind["t"] == "machine":
            if fingerprint is None:
                return _invalid(Reason.BINDING_MISMATCH, "no fingerprint supplied")
            if machine_binding(fingerprint) != bind["val"]:
                return _invalid(Reason.BINDING_MISMATCH,
                                "fingerprint does not match license binding")

        min_v = parse_version(p["min_v"])
        if client_version < min_v:
            return _invalid(Reason.MIN_VERSION,
                            f"client {'.'.join(map(str, client_version))} "
                            f"< min_v {p['min_v']}")

        # 4. revocation --------------------------------------------------------
        if p["ser"] in revoked_serials:
            return _invalid(Reason.REVOKED, f"ser={p['ser']}")

        # 5. anti-rollback -----------------------------------------------------
        if state is not None and p["ser"] <= state.high_water_serial:
            return _invalid(Reason.SERIAL_ROLLBACK,
                            f"ser={p['ser']} <= high-water={state.high_water_serial}")

        return _valid()

    except StructureError as exc:
        return _invalid(Reason.STRUCTURE, str(exc))
    except Exception as exc:  # fail-closed: the unexpected path must never allow
        return _invalid(Reason.INTERNAL, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""License test harness: issues test licenses with a TEST key, then attacks them.

The issuer side lives HERE (test tooling only). The shipped client module
(licverify.py) contains no private key and no signing code -- signing belongs
to the HSM-backed service, never to the application.

Run:  .venv/bin/python harness.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import sys

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

import licverify as lv

# fixed clock for reproducibility
NOW = 1_750_000_000
NB = 1_700_000_000
NA = 1_800_000_000
FP_A = "mb:AA-BB-CC:disk-001:mac-deadbeef"   # this machine
FP_B = "mb:11-22-33:disk-999:mac-cafebabe"   # someone else's box
KID_A = "acme-x/2026a"
KID_B = "acme-x/2026b"
KID_FUTURE = "acme-x/2027a"


# ---- issuer side (test only) ------------------------------------------------

def issue(priv, kid, payload) -> bytes:
    header = {"v": 1, "kid": kid, "alg": "Ed25519"}
    sig = priv.sign(lv.signed_scope(header, payload))
    env = {"h": header, "p": payload, "s": base64.b64encode(sig).decode("ascii")}
    return json.dumps(env).encode("utf-8")


def base_payload() -> dict:
    return {
        "lic": "ACME-00012345-47",
        "ser": 47,
        "iss": "vendor:acme",
        "prod": {"id": "acme-x", "ed": "pro", "feats": {"export": 1, "batch": 0}},
        "cust": {"id": "org:1234", "name": "Example Ltd"},
        "lim": {"seats": 5, "conc": 2, "vol": None},
        "term": {"perp": False, "nb": NB, "na": NA, "grace_d": 14, "off_d": 30},
        "bind": {"t": "machine", "val": lv.machine_binding(FP_A), "drift": "2of3"},
        "min_v": "9.4.0",
    }


# ---- one test case ----------------------------------------------------------

def run_case(name, blob, *, want, keyring, now=NOW, fingerprint=FP_A,
             client_version=(9, 4, 1), state=None, revoked=frozenset()) -> bool:
    res = lv.verify_license(
        blob, keyring, now=now, fingerprint=fingerprint,
        client_version=client_version, state=state, revoked_serials=revoked,
    )
    ok = (res.verdict, res.reason) == want
    tag = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    line = f"  [{tag}] {name}: {res.verdict.value}/{res.reason.value}"
    if res.detail:
        line += f" -- {res.detail}"
    if not ok:
        line += f"   EXPECTED {want[0].value}/{want[1].value}"
    print(line)
    return ok


def main() -> int:
    priv_a = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    priv_b = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    impostor = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    ring = lv.Keyring({KID_A: priv_a.public_key(), KID_B: priv_b.public_key()})

    good = issue(priv_a, KID_A, base_payload())

    print("license verification harness\n")
    results: list[bool] = []

    # T01 baseline -- valid license, right machine, current client
    results.append(run_case(
        "T01 valid license, this machine", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.VALID, lv.Reason.OK), keyring=ring))

    # T02 cosmetic re-serialization: whitespace + key order change is fine --
    # the verifier rebuilds canonical bytes from the parsed object, so the
    # signed scope is identical. (What is NOT fine: duplicate keys, T12.)
    env2 = json.loads(good)
    shuffled = json.dumps({"s": env2["s"], "p": env2["p"], "h": env2["h"]},
                          indent=4).encode()
    results.append(run_case(
        "T02 cosmetic re-serialization still verifies", shuffled,
        want=(lv.Verdict.VALID, lv.Reason.OK), keyring=ring))

    # T03 payload tamper: seats 5 -> 500, signature untouched
    env3 = json.loads(good)
    env3["p"]["lim"]["seats"] = 500
    results.append(run_case(
        "T03 payload tamper (seats 5->500)", json.dumps(env3).encode(),
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.BAD_SIGNATURE), keyring=ring))

    # T04 header swap: kid A -> B (both keys pinned). Header is inside the
    # signed scope, so the swap breaks the signature.
    env4 = json.loads(good)
    env4["h"]["kid"] = KID_B
    results.append(run_case(
        "T04 header swap (kid A->B)", json.dumps(env4).encode(),
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.BAD_SIGNATURE), keyring=ring))

    # T05 unknown kid: signed by a real key, but kid not in this client's
    # keyring -> INDETERMINATE with upgrade hint, never silent allow.
    foreign = issue(priv_a, KID_FUTURE, base_payload())
    results.append(run_case(
        "T05 unknown kid (future key)", foreign,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INDETERMINATE, lv.Reason.UNKNOWN_KID), keyring=ring))

    # T06 expired
    results.append(run_case(
        "T06 expired license", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.EXPIRED), keyring=ring, now=NA + 1))

    # T07 not yet valid
    results.append(run_case(
        "T07 not yet valid", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.NOT_YET_VALID), keyring=ring, now=NB - 1))

    # T08 wrong machine fingerprint
    results.append(run_case(
        "T08 other machine", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.BINDING_MISMATCH), keyring=ring,
        fingerprint=FP_B))

    # T09 replay: this serial was already accepted on this seat (high-water 47)
    st9 = lv.LocalState(high_water_serial=47, last_seen_time=NOW)
    results.append(run_case(
        "T09 replay of used serial", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.SERIAL_ROLLBACK), keyring=ring, state=st9))

    # T10 clock rollback: corroborated high-water is 10 days ahead of `now`
    st10 = lv.LocalState(last_seen_time=NOW + 10 * 86400)
    results.append(run_case(
        "T10 clock rollback", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INDETERMINATE, lv.Reason.CLOCK_ROLLBACK), keyring=ring,
        state=st10))

    # T11 client below min version
    results.append(run_case(
        "T11 client below min_v", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.MIN_VERSION), keyring=ring,
        client_version=(9, 3, 0)))

    # T12 duplicate JSON keys -- parse must reject, no last-wins ambiguity
    dup = b'{"h":{"v":1,"kid":"acme-x/2026a","alg":"Ed25519"},"h":{},"p":{},"s":""}'
    results.append(run_case(
        "T12 duplicate JSON keys", dup,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.STRUCTURE), keyring=ring))

    # T13 oversized blob -- rejected before parsing
    results.append(run_case(
        "T13 oversized blob", b"x" * (lv.MAX_LICENSE_BYTES + 1),
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.TOO_LARGE), keyring=ring))

    # T14 impostor: signs with its own key but claims a pinned kid
    imp = issue(impostor, KID_A, base_payload())
    results.append(run_case(
        "T14 impostor keypair", imp,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.BAD_SIGNATURE), keyring=ring))

    # T15 perpetual license: no na, still valid far past the nominal date
    pp = base_payload()
    pp["term"] = {"perp": True, "nb": NB, "na": None, "grace_d": 14, "off_d": 30}
    perp = issue(priv_a, KID_A, pp)
    results.append(run_case(
        "T15 perpetual past nominal date", perp,
        want=(lv.Verdict.VALID, lv.Reason.OK), keyring=ring, now=NA + 10_000_000))

    # T16 revoked serial
    results.append(run_case(
        "T16 revoked serial", good,
        want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.REVOKED), keyring=ring,
        revoked=frozenset({47})))

    passed = sum(results)
    print(f"\n{passed}/{len(results)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(results) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extra fail-closed sweep: mutations and junk must NEVER yield VALID,
and verify_license must never raise -- on anything."""
import json
import random
import string

import licverify as lv
import harness as H
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

random.seed(1337)
priv = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
ring = lv.Keyring({H.KID_A: priv.public_key()})
good = H.issue(priv, H.KID_A, H.base_payload())

valid_hits = 0
checks = 0

# 1. every single-character mutation inside the base64 signature region
env = json.loads(good)
sig = env["s"]
b64_alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "+/"
for i in range(len(sig)):
    for _ in range(3):
        ch = random.choice(b64_alphabet)
        if ch == sig[i]:
            continue
        mutated = sig[:i] + ch + sig[i + 1:]
        blob = json.dumps({"h": env["h"], "p": env["p"], "s": mutated}).encode()
        res = lv.verify_license(blob, ring, now=H.NOW, fingerprint=H.FP_A)
        checks += 1
        if res.ok:
            valid_hits += 1

# 2. payload value mutations (signed content) -- must all fail at the sig gate
for i in range(300):
    e = json.loads(good)
    e["p"]["ser"] = random.randint(1, 10**9)
    blob = json.dumps(e).encode()
    res = lv.verify_license(blob, ring, now=H.NOW, fingerprint=H.FP_A)
    checks += 1
    if res.ok:
        valid_hits += 1

# 3. junk corpus -- no exceptions allowed, no VALID allowed
junk = [
    b"", b" ", b"\x00", b"null", b"[]", b"{}", b'"a"', b"123",
    b"{", b"}", b'{"h":{}}', b'{"h":{"v":1},"p":{},"s":""}',
    b'{"h":{"v":1,"kid":"x","alg":"Ed25519"},"p":[],"s":"AA=="}',
    b'{"h":{"v":1,"kid":"x","alg":"Ed25519"},"p":{},"s":"' + b"A" * 400 + b'"}',
    b'{"h":{"v":1,"kid":"x","alg":"Ed25519"},"p":{},"s":"AA==\nBB=="}',
    bytes(random.randrange(256) for _ in range(64)),
    bytes(random.randrange(256) for _ in range(4096)),
]
raised = 0
for blob in junk:
    try:
        res = lv.verify_license(blob, ring, now=H.NOW, fingerprint=H.FP_A)
        checks += 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Test keystore generator for the license harness (series part 2, in code).

Layout produced under --dir:
  root.pem              offline root private key (0600). First job here: sign
                        the keyring manifest. Leaf delegation certs come with
                        the chain slice.
  leaf-<kid-slug>.pem   per-epoch license signing keys (0600)
  keyring.pub.json      kid -> public key: what the client pins
                        (raw ed25519 bytes, base64 + sha256 fingerprint)
  keyring.sig.json      root signature over the canonical keyring body

Harness-grade: file-based keys, mode 0600, refuses to overwrite. Production
keeps the root in an HSM and leaves inside a signing service -- this module is
the test twin of that setup.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
    Ed25519PrivateKey,
    Ed25519PublicKey,
)

import licverify as lv

ROOT_KID = "root/2026"
LEAF_KIDS_DEFAULT = ["acme-x/2026a", "acme-x/2026b"]  # epoch + next slot
KEYRING_DOMAIN = b"keyring-v1\x00"


def _slug(kid: str) -> str:
    return kid.replace("/", "_")


def _write_private(path: Path, key: Ed25519PrivateKey) -> None:
    path.write_bytes(key.private_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.PEM,
        serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
        serialization.NoEncryption(),
    ))
    os.chmod(path, 0o600)


def _pub_record(kid: str, pub) -> dict:
    raw = pub.public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.Raw,
                           serialization.PublicFormat.Raw)
    return {
        "kid": kid,
        "alg": "Ed25519",
        "pub_b64": base64.b64encode(raw).decode("ascii"),
        "pub_sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
    }


def generate(keydir, leaf_kids=None, force=False) -> dict:
    keydir = Path(keydir)
    keydir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    leaf_kids = leaf_kids or LEAF_KIDS_DEFAULT
    if not force and any(keydir.glob("*.pem")):
        raise FileExistsError(f"{keydir} already holds keys (use --force)")

    root = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    _write_private(keydir / "root.pem", root)

    body = {"v": 1, "root_kid": ROOT_KID, "keys": {}}
    for kid in leaf_kids:
        leaf = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
        _write_private(keydir / f"leaf-{_slug(kid)}.pem", leaf)
        body["keys"][kid] = _pub_record(kid, leaf.public_key())

    (keydir / "keyring.pub.json").write_text(json.dumps(body, indent=2) + "\n")

    # root's first job: sign the keyring manifest so a swapped file is detectable
    sig = root.sign(KEYRING_DOMAIN + lv.canonical_bytes(body))
    (keydir / "keyring.sig.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "alg": "Ed25519",
        "root_kid": ROOT_KID,
        "sig_b64": base64.b64encode(sig).decode("ascii"),
    }, indent=2) + "\n")

    return body


# ---- loading (issuer side + demo self-checks) --------------------------------

def load_leaf(keydir, kid: str):
    pem = (Path(keydir) / f"leaf-{_slug(kid)}.pem").read_bytes()
    return serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem, password=None)


def load_public_keyring(keydir) -> "lv.Keyring":
    body = json.loads((Path(keydir) / "keyring.pub.json").read_text())
    keys = {}
    for kid, rec in body["keys"].items():
        if rec.get("alg") != "Ed25519":
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported alg for {kid!r}: {rec.get('alg')!r}")
        keys[kid] = Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(
            base64.b64decode(rec["pub_b64"]))
    return lv.Keyring(keys)


def verify_keyring_manifest(keydir) -> bool:
    """Self-check twin of the client-side manifest check that lands with the
    chain slice. Client will pin the root PUBLIC key as a constant; here we
    lift it from root.pem since the harness keeps the whole keystore."""
    keydir = Path(keydir)
    body = json.loads((keydir / "keyring.pub.json").read_text())
    sig_rec = json.loads((keydir / "keyring.sig.json").read_text())
    root = serialization.load_pem_private_key(
        (keydir / "root.pem").read_bytes(), password=None)
    try:
        root.public_key().verify(
            base64.b64decode(sig_rec["sig_b64"]),
            KEYRING_DOMAIN + lv.canonical_bytes(body))
        return True
    except InvalidSignature:
        return False


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="generate test keystore")
    ap.add_argument("--dir", default=str(Path(__file__).parent / "keys"))
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        body = generate(args.dir, force=args.force)
    except FileExistsError as exc:
        print(f"refusing: {exc}")
        return 2

    print(f"keystore: {args.dir}")
    for kid, rec in body["keys"].items():
        print(f"  leaf {kid}  pub_sha256 {rec['pub_sha256'][:16]}...")
    print(f"  root {ROOT_KID}  keyring manifest signed -> keyring.sig.json")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""License issuance for the test harness: order -> payload -> signed blob.

Deliberately imports licverify.signed_scope and licverify.machine_binding:
issuer and client share ONE canonicalization implementation here, so the
verify-vs-use differential has nowhere to hide in the harness. (A real vendor
issuer lives in another codebase; there the discipline is golden test vectors
plus a frozen format spec.)

Usage:
  .venv/bin/python issuance.py demo
  .venv/bin/python issuance.py issue --kid acme-x/2026a --days 90 --out lic/x.lic
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import keygen as kg
import licverify as lv

HARNESS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent
KEYDIR = HARNESS_DIR / "keys"
LICDIR = HARNESS_DIR / "lic"
FP_DEFAULT = "mb:AA-BB-CC:disk-001:mac-deadbeef"
FP_OTHER = "mb:11-22-33:disk-999:mac-cafebabe"
DAY = 86_400


# ---- order -> payload -> blob ----------------------------------------------

def make_order(lic="ACME-00012345", cust_id="org:1234", cust_name="Example Ltd",
               ed="pro", feats=None, seats=5, conc=2, days=365, perp=False,
               grace_d=14, off_d=30, min_v="9.4.0", fp=FP_DEFAULT) -> dict:
    return {"lic": lic, "cust_id": cust_id, "cust_name": cust_name, "ed": ed,
            "feats": feats or {"export": 1, "batch": 0}, "seats": seats,
            "conc": conc, "days": days, "perp": perp, "grace_d": grace_d,
            "off_d": off_d, "min_v": min_v, "fp": fp}


def build_payload(order: dict, *, now: int, serial: int) -> dict:
    """Order spec -> wire payload. Field set mirrors licverify's schema exactly."""
    perp = bool(order["perp"])
    return {
        "lic": order["lic"],
        "ser": serial,
        "iss": lv.ISSUER,
        "prod": {"id": lv.PRODUCT_ID, "ed": order["ed"],
                 "feats": dict(order["feats"])},
        "cust": {"id": order["cust_id"], "name": order["cust_name"]},
        "lim": {"seats": order["seats"], "conc": order["conc"], "vol": None},
        "term": {"perp": perp, "nb": now,
                 "na": None if perp else now + order["days"] * DAY,
                 "grace_d": order["grace_d"], "off_d": order["off_d"]},
        "bind": {"t": "machine", "val": lv.machine_binding(order["fp"]),
                 "drift": "2of3"},
        "min_v": order["min_v"],
    }


def issue_blob(leaf_priv, kid: str, payload: dict) -> bytes:
    header = {"v": 1, "kid": kid, "alg": "Ed25519"}
    sig = leaf_priv.sign(lv.signed_scope(header, payload))
    return json.dumps({
        "h": header,
        "p": payload,
        "s": base64.b64encode(sig).decode("ascii"),
    }).encode("utf-8")


class SerialLedger:
    """Per-license serial high-water, persisted. Reissues increment; the
    client's anti-rollback check (part 5) keys off exactly this counter."""

    def __init__(self, path, start: int = 47):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.start = start
        self.data = json.loads(self.path.read_text()) if self.path.exists() else {}

    def next(self, lic: str) -> int:
        if lic in self.data:
            self.data[lic] += 1
        else:
            self.data[lic] = self.start
        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(self.data, indent=2) + "\n")
        return self.data[lic]


def issue_from_keydir(keydir, kid: str, order: dict, *, now: int,
                      ledger: SerialLedger, out=None):
    leaf = kg.load_leaf(keydir, kid)
    payload = build_payload(order, now=now, serial=ledger.next(order["lic"]))
    blob = issue_blob(leaf, kid, payload)
    if out is not None:
        out = Path(out)
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_bytes(blob)
    return payload, blob


# ---- demo -------------------------------------------------------------------

def _check(name, blob, *, want, ring, now, fp=FP_DEFAULT, state=None) -> bool:
    res = lv.verify_license(blob, ring, now=now, fingerprint=fp,
                            client_version=(9, 4, 1), state=state)
    ok = (res.verdict, res.reason) == want
    line = (f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}: "
            f"{res.verdict.value}/{res.reason.value}")
    if res.detail:
        line += f" -- {res.detail}"
    if not ok:
        line += f"   EXPECTED {want[0].value}/{want[1].value}"
    print(line)
    return ok


def demo() -> int:
    now = 1_750_000_000
    keydir = KEYDIR
    if not (keydir / "root.pem").exists():
        kg.generate(keydir)
        print(f"generated fresh test keys in {keydir}")

    ring = kg.load_public_keyring(keydir)
    print(f"keyring manifest verified: {kg.verify_keyring_manifest(keydir)}")
    print(f"pinned kids: {', '.join(sorted(ring.keys))}\n")

    led_path = HARNESS_DIR / "issuer-state" / "demo-ledger.json"
    led_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)          # deterministic serials per run
    led = SerialLedger(led_path, start=47)
    LICDIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    results: list[bool] = []
    order = make_order()

    # D1 mint serial 47 on the current epoch key, verify as this machine
    p47, blob47 = issue_from_keydir(keydir, "acme-x/2026a", order, now=now,
                                   ledger=led, out=LICDIR / "ACME-00012345-s47.lic")
    print(f"  blob head: {blob47[:220].decode()}...\n")
    st = lv.LocalState()
    results.append(_check("D1 minted ser47 verifies", blob47,
                          want=(lv.Verdict.VALID, lv.Reason.OK),
                          ring=ring, now=now, state=st))
    st.commit(p47["ser"], now)

    # D2 reissue -> serial bumps; client state advances
    p48, blob48 = issue_from_keydir(keydir, "acme-x/2026a", order, now=now,
                                   ledger=led, out=LICDIR / "ACME-00012345-s48.lic")
    results.append(_check("D2 reissue ser48 verifies", blob48,
                          want=(lv.Verdict.VALID, lv.Reason.OK),
                          ring=ring, now=now, state=st))
    st.commit(p48["ser"], now)

    # D3 replay of the old blob is now blocked by the anti-rollback high-water
    results.append(_check("D3 replay of ser47 blocked", blob47,
                          want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.SERIAL_ROLLBACK),
                          ring=ring, now=now, state=st))

    # D4 rotation slot: next epoch key routes fine through the same keyring
    order_b = make_order(lic="ACME-00099999")
    _, blob_b = issue_from_keydir(keydir, "acme-x/2026b", order_b, now=now,
                                  ledger=led, out=LICDIR / "ACME-00099999-s47.lic")
    results.append(_check("D4 next-epoch key (2026b) verifies", blob_b,
                          want=(lv.Verdict.VALID, lv.Reason.OK),
                          ring=ring, now=now))

    # D5 a kid the keyring does not know -> indeterminate, upgrade hint
    payload_x = build_payload(make_order(lic="ACME-00077777"), now=now, serial=1)
    blob_x = issue_blob(kg.load_leaf(keydir, "acme-x/2026b"), "acme-x/2027a", payload_x)
    results.append(_check("D5 unknown kid 2027a", blob_x,
                          want=(lv.Verdict.INDETERMINATE, lv.Reason.UNKNOWN_KID),
                          ring=ring, now=now))

    # D6 same blob on another machine
    results.append(_check("D6 wrong machine fingerprint", blob48,
                          want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.BINDING_MISMATCH),
                          ring=ring, now=now, fp=FP_OTHER))

    # D7 short-term license, verified after expiry
    order_e = make_order(lic="ACME-00054321", days=1)
    _, blob_e = issue_from_keydir(keydir, "acme-x/2026a", order_e, now=now,
                                  ledger=led, out=LICDIR / "ACME-00054321-s47.lic")
    results.append(_check("D7 expired after 2 days", blob_e,
                          want=(lv.Verdict.INVALID, lv.Reason.EXPIRED),
                          ring=ring, now=now + 2 * DAY))

    passed = sum(results)
    print(f"\n{passed}/{len(results)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(results) else 1


# ---- CLI ---------------------------------------------------------------------

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="license issuance (harness)")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd")
    sub.add_parser("demo", help="end-to-end mint + verify demo")

    p = sub.add_parser("issue", help="mint one license")
    p.add_argument("--kid", default="acme-x/2026a")
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--lic", default="ACME-00012345")
    p.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=365)
    p.add_argument("--perp", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--seats", type=int, default=5)
    p.add_argument("--now", type=int, default=1_750_000_000)
    p.add_argument("--fp", default=FP_DEFAULT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd in (None, "demo"):
        return demo()

    if not (KEYDIR / "root.pem").exists():
        print(f"no keystore in {KEYDIR}; run: python keygen.py")
        return 2
    led = SerialLedger(HARNESS_DIR / "issuer-state" / "serial-ledger.json")
    order = make_order(lic=args.lic, days=args.days, perp=args.perp,
                       seats=args.seats, fp=args.fp)
    payload, _ = issue_from_keydir(KEYDIR, args.kid, order, now=args.now,
                                   ledger=led, out=args.out)
    print(f"issued {args.lic} ser={payload['ser']} kid={args.kid} -> {args.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Part seven 🔬 — tamper lab built, and it earned its keep immediately. First run caught a bug in my lab code, not the scheme: every demo was denied at `invalid/min_version` because the lab's calls forgot to pass `client_version` and the verifier's fail-closed default `(0,0,0)` refused everything. Fixed the lab, re-ran: 8/8 replacement paths reach the decision layer, and the attack suite still passes 16/16 after (all patches restored).

THE FRAME FIRST — TAMPERING BY TIER

  Tier 0  black-box: attacker touches only blob/files/network bytes
          -> everything holds. Edits, header swaps, truncation, garbage: structure + signature eat them
             (suite T01-T16, 579-input sweep: zero VALID, zero crashes)
  Tier 1  gray-box: attacker gets in-process / on-host reach
          -> everything local is replacement-addressable. 8/8 demos below walk through
  Tier 2  keys: steal the leaf private key -> game over for that epoch; nothing else needed
          -> every Tier 1 win goes AROUND the math, never through it

So the failure model isn't "the crypto breaks". It's "which components does the attacker replace, and how reachable is each replacement". That's what the lab audits, and that's the researcher's test map:

  REPLACED COMPONENT      HARNESS TWIN (today)              COMPILED-PRODUCT TWIN
  verifier decision       lv.verify_license hook            branch patch / NOP the call
  crypto call             fake key.verify()                 hook EVP_DigestVerify / Frida
  pin set                 swap keyring.pub.json             patch embedded bytes / hook loader
  time source             the `now` argument                host clock / hook time()
  state store             FrozenState / state file          delete or snapshot-rollback state
  binding input           patch machine_binding             hook the HWID APIs it samples
  signed-scope shape      narrow signed_scope               ship the build that omits a field (bug class)
  consumed bytes          consumer re-read                  TOCTOU in the app's own call flow
